text:
Will Smith has 14 points in 21 games for San Jose, and our numbers think that undersells him. The Sharks have scored 5.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists, and his scoring rate of 2.01 points per 60 sits below the low end of the range our talent model gives him.

The chances are there. He has 7 goals on 8.6 expected, shooting right around his normal rate, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 98th percentile among forwards for chances from the slot last season, often off passes across the royal road. He's playing 20 minutes a night at 21, in his third NHL season, and the Sharks are better at five on five with him than without him, if still under water overall.

The power play has been a sore spot. He talked about its struggles after a loss in Dallas, though he scored on it that night. Evolving-Hockey's knock from last season was defensive: opponents generated more against him than against most forwards. The finishing and the setup are fine. Watch his line's defensive numbers, and watch the assists, which should start arriving.
headline: Will Smith is better than his point total
